title: An agent logo skill that tests every mark at 16 pixels
summary: An agent logo skill that tests every mark at 16 pixels, one colour and against a competitor shelf, then stops so you pick a concept before it builds the kit: https://github.com/kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill
body_markdown:
An agent can draw you a logo. This skill adds the checks a designer runs before showing one: 16 px, one colour, and next to competitors. logo-design-skill, from kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill, makes the agent work like an identity designer: write a brief, research the category, draw concepts in SVG, then test them the way a designer would.

It works in Claude and in any agent that supports the Agent Skills format, including Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor and GitHub Copilot.

## A process that stops at a checkpoint

The flow runs in five stages. It starts with a brief, from your answers or from assumptions it states, researches the category's conventions, writes 8 to 12 one-line concepts and builds 3 of them in SVG, tests and refines those, and then reaches a checkpoint.

At the checkpoint the skill always stops. It shows the concepts as one overview image, in greyscale at true 64, 32 and 16 px sizes, with a recommendation, and offers the full kit. Nothing else gets made until you pick a direction. The kit, which covers colour, lockups, a presentation board, icons and guidelines, is most of the work, so it only makes sense for an idea you have approved.

The examples back up why that stop matters. The project ran 28 fictional briefs end to end, from a specialty coffee roaster to a password manager. In four of the latest ten, the client picked a different concept than the one the skill recommended, and the skill refined that choice before colouring it.

## Tests a designer would run

The tools are dependency-free Python. One audits an SVG against logo principles. Others build concept overview sheets and test sheets:

- a 16 px pixel test
- one-colour and reversed versions
- a squint test and a mirror test
- the mark in context
- a competitor shelf test

There are also tools to build client presentation boards with industry-specific mockups, render PNGs, and export a full favicon, app-icon and web-manifest set. The skill works best with a model that can view images, because it renders its own drafts to PNG and checks them before showing you.

The later example batches push vivid, saturated palettes while still passing the one-colour and 3:1 contrast checks. The newest batch takes on three crowded categories with explicit cliches to avoid: no chat bubbles, charts or padlocks for SaaS, no coins, piggy banks or bank blue for finance, and no crosses, pills or heartbeat lines for health.

## A reference library, used to avoid look-alikes

The skill ships a library of more than 1,400 real-world SVG logos, each classified by mark type, technique, geometry, subject, typography, mood and industry. You can search it from the command line or browse it in a local gallery. The stated use is to study construction, map what a category usually looks like and avoid look-alikes, never to copy. I would want that check before showing any mark to a client.

The principles section covers word mapping, choosing the right mark type, geometric construction, and optical corrections such as overshoot, the bone effect and irradiation.

## Installing it

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill
/plugin install logo-design@logo-design-skill
```

For Claude.ai or Claude Desktop, upload `logo-design.zip` from the Releases page under Settings, Capabilities, Skills, or `logo-design-lite.zip` if you hit a size limit. For other agents, copy the `skills/logo-design` folder into the agent's skills directory. Then start a new session and ask for a logo. I would give it a real brief for something you have already branded and see whether the shelf test flags the same neighbours you worried about.
